subject: Fleet fitment brief: proposed hybrid H100/A100/L4 mix for FormaHealth Dedicated
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Becker <tom.becker@formahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet fitment brief: initial usage details and ask

Tom / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our chat, I’ve pulled together the baseline usage profile so we can converge on a Dedicated fleet recommendation that matches performance needs and your cost targets. Attached: usage_report_q1.csv (sampled request rates, median/95th token counts, and model mix).

Quick summary of what you told us and what we need to confirm:
- Target latency SLOs: 95p generation latency < 800ms for chat models on primary routes. Embeddings < 150ms.
- Peak concurrency: ~220 concurrent requests during business hours; steady-state ~40 QPS across all routes.
- Model types: two heavy generation models (Vicuna-70B style, long-context ~16k tokens), one mid-size chat (13B), and embeddings workload (real-time, short contexts).
- Cost target: reduce per-token inference cost vs current self-hosted baseline by ~30% after optimization.

Immediate asks for sizing: can you confirm the expected 95th prompt length distribution (we have a draft in the CSV), and whether you expect bursts >3x baseline for product launches? Also confirm whether audit logs retention beyond 90 days is required (affects Private vs Dedicated design).

We’ll coordinate a short follow-up with Dev and Rishi to propose a hybrid fleet mix (H100 + A100 + L4) and suggested autoscaling policy.

Next step: if you’re comfortable, can you share a signed NDA and we’ll run an internal sizing simulation against your Q1 traces? We can turn around a recommended fleet + cost estimate in 3 business days.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fleet fitment brief: initial usage details and ask

Marissa —

Thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- 95p prompt length for the heavy generator is typically ~7.5k tokens (we do have occasional 16k outliers for transcript summarization, ~1% of traffic).
- We do expect product-driven bursts: marketing campaigns historically created ~4x traffic for 48–72 hours; capacity should be able to handle 2x without manual ops-intervention, with documented fallback plan for 4x.
- Audit logs: yes, we need 180-day retention for audit trails (HIPAA-related recordkeeping).

On the timeline — NDA is in legal review, but we can fast-track. Once we sign, happy to provide the full trace export.

One question up front: you mentioned H100 and L4 in the overview. Can you summarize the tradeoffs we should expect — specifically memory headroom for the 70B-style model and whether an L4-based pool can realistically carry your embedding load at the latency we require?

Best,
Tom
VP Product, FormaHealth

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Becker <tom.becker@formahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet fitment brief: initial usage details and ask

Tom / Marissa —

Thanks for the clarity, Tom. High-level technical tradeoffs and a proposed fitment strategy below. I’ll attach the modeling workbook (fleet_mix_modeling.xlsx) with assumptions and simulated cost/latency curves for your traces.

Short answers:
- H100 (80GB) — best fit for your 70B-style long-context generator. Memory headroom matters once you include KV cache + 16k context; with 80GB H100 in a single-socket config we can run the model with room for a reasonable batch (batch=1–2 for low latency) and partial KV caching across requests. This gives the best 95p latency and most predictable tail behavior.
- A100 (40/80GB variants) — still a good general-purpose SKU. 80GB A100 can host a 70B model but with tighter headroom vs H100 and potentially higher kernel-exec latency depending on compiled kernels. A100 is attractive if you want higher density and lower per-card hourly cost in some cloud vendors.
- L4 (24 GB) — purpose-built for cheaper, high-volume, short-context workloads: embeddings and small chat models. It won’t host the 70B long-context generator reliably at scale, but it can carry all embedding requests and mid-size 13B chat in quantized form (int8/llm.int4) with substantial cost savings.

Proposed fleet mix (initial pilot):
- H100 pool: 12 cards (2 racks equivalent) reserved for heavy generation; configured with preference routing for requests labeled "long_context_gen"; autoscale cushion +20% headroom to absorb 2x bursts.
- L4 pool: 24 cards dedicated to embeddings + 13B quantized chat; aggressive batching for embeddings, with streaming turned off for bulk offline embed jobs.
- A100 utility pool: 8 cards for overflow and model variants (fallback when H100 latency SLOs are at risk).

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- Memory vs throughput: H100 gives memory headroom but is more expensive per-card. A100 80GB is closer on memory but trades off higher kernel latency and less future-proofing for very long contexts. L4 wins on cost per embedding request but requires quantization and more careful evals to ensure quality parity.
- KV cache and prefix caching: we recommend per-tenant KV cache in Dedicated (persistent between requests on the same host). This reduces tokens generated per request for repeated prompts and improves effective throughput—important for your transcript summarization where prefixes repeat.
- Autoscaling: prefer a hybrid policy: keep H100 at a modest reserved baseline to satisfy SLOs and scale A100/L4 for pooling. Implement policy-based fallback (route to A100 with lower batch sizes) before rejecting requests.
- Audit/logging: 180-day retention can be supported on Dedicated; this will increase storage and egress costs (see workbook).

I attached the workbook with cost curves and sensitivity tests (peak 2x vs 4x). Recommendation summary on sheet 'Executive': pilot mixed pool (H100 + L4) and use A100 as burst/fallback. If you prefer a single SKU for contractual simplicity, A100-80GB is the middle-ground but expect higher tail latency on long-context workloads.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the modeling.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: fleet_mix_modeling.xlsx (XLSX, 220 KB)

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet fitment brief: proposed hybrid H100/A100/L4 mix for FormaHealth Dedicated

Tom —

Thanks for the quick review and for flagging retention needs. Based on Dev’s workbook and the traces you’ll share post-NDA, here’s the proposed mutual action plan so we can lock capacity and pricing: 

1) NDA & trace export (FormaHealth legal): sign by EOD Friday (you mentioned fast-track) — Redwood will run the simulation.
2) Pilot PO for Dedicated Reserved: H100 pool (12 cards) + L4 pool (24 cards) + A100 utility (8 cards). Term: 6 months trial with opt-out window at month 3.
3) Deliverables from Redwood within 3 business days of trace: detailed cost estimate, bolstered runbook (KV cache config, autoscale thresholds, fallback routing), and SLA appendix reflecting 95p latency targets.
4) Pricing: draft attached (pricing-draft-FormaHealth.pdf). The pilot pricing assumes a blended reserved rate with usage overage discounts; detailed numbers in the workbook depend on selected burst cushion.
4) Ops readiness: Rishi will own initial deployment and monitoring (alerts on latency, cache hit-rate, failover tests).

If this plan looks good, please confirm and I’ll get the PO template to you. We’ll also include a clause to revisit SKU composition at month 3 based on observed model mix (e.g., convert some A100 to H100 if 70B long-context demand grows).

If you want a single-sku simplification instead: we can propose A100-80GB only, but Dev’s analysis shows noticeable tail risk on long-context workloads compared to H100.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
